# Project Guidelines — BMS-Firmware-RTOS

## Overview
STM32L432KC FreeRTOS firmware for a battery management system monitoring 18 cells (two BQ76952 ICs) and 56 thermistors, communicating over CAN bus. Supports up to 16 identical modules via flash-stored module ID.

## Code Style
- **C only** (not C++), compiled with `arm-none-eabi-gcc`, `-Wall`, `-Og` debug builds.
- Functions: `PascalCase` with module prefix — `CAN_SendMessage()`, `BQ_ReadBMS1()`, `ErrorMgr_SetError()`.
- Types: `typedef` with `_t` suffix — `BMS_State_t`, `CAN_Message_t`.
- Enums: `TYPE_VALUE` — `BMS_STATE_INIT`, `ERROR_OVER_VOLTAGE`.
- Defines/constants: `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` with module prefix.
- Globals use `g_` prefix. Include guards use `#ifndef __HEADER_H` with `extern "C"` wrapping.
- Doxygen on all public functions (`@brief`, `@param`, `@retval`). Trailing `/**< */` on struct fields.
- See [Core/Src/can_manager.c](Core/Src/can_manager.c) and [Core/Inc/bq_handler.h](Core/Inc/bq_handler.h) for exemplary style.

## Architecture
- **FreeRTOS** (CMSIS-RTOS V2 wrapper): 5 tasks, preemptive, 1ms tick, heap_4 (12KB).
- **Tasks**: `BQ_MonitorTask` ×2 (cell voltages, prio 40), `CellTemp_MonitorTask` (thermistors, prio 40), `CAN_ManagerTask` (TX/RX queues, prio 56), `BMSResetHandlerTask` (prio 8).
- **Shared resources**: Every shared variable is mutex-protected (`osMutexWait`/`osMutexRelease`, `osWaitForever`). Two I2C mutexes, state mutex, error mutex, config mutex, voltage mutexes.
- **State machine**: INIT → IDLE → CHARGING / DISCHARGING / BALANCING / ERROR. ERROR state locks while faults active. See [Core/Src/state_machine.c](Core/Src/state_machine.c).
- **Error system**: 32-bit error + 32-bit warning flags across 4 bytes (Temp/Voltage/Current/Comm). See [Core/Inc/error_manager.h](Core/Inc/error_manager.h).
- **CAN addressing**: 29-bit extended IDs, module ID in bits 15:12. All IDs computed at runtime via `CAN_ID(base, module)` macro in [Core/Inc/can_ids.h](Core/Inc/can_ids.h).
- **Dual BQ76952**: Identical I2C address `0x08` on separate buses (I2C1, I2C3). Each has its own task and mutex.

## Build and Test
```bash
# Build (via VS Code tasks — preferred)
# Use task "Build STM" or "Build Clean STM" from the command palette

# Build via terminal (PowerShell, from repo root)
& "$env:APPDATA\Code\User\globalStorage\bmd.stm32-for-vscode\@xpack-dev-tools\windows-build-tools\4.4.1-3.1\.content\bin\make.EXE" -j16 DEBUG=1 -f STM32Make.make

# Clean + rebuild via terminal (PowerShell)
& "$env:APPDATA\Code\User\globalStorage\bmd.stm32-for-vscode\@xpack-dev-tools\windows-build-tools\4.4.1-3.1\.content\bin\make.EXE" clean -f STM32Make.make
& "$env:APPDATA\Code\User\globalStorage\bmd.stm32-for-vscode\@xpack-dev-tools\windows-build-tools\4.4.1-3.1\.content\bin\make.EXE" -j16 DEBUG=1 -f STM32Make.make

# Notes:
# - .stm32env supplies ARM_GCC_PATH/OPENOCD and should use $(USERPROFILE)-based paths.
# - If tool versions change, update the version segment in the make/openocd paths above.

# Flash via OpenOCD
# Use task "Flash STM", or: openocd -f openocd.cfg

# Generate DBC file (after CAN protocol changes)
python Scripts/generate_dbc.py

# Flash firmware over CAN (bootloader)
python Scripts/Flash_Application.py
```
No unit test framework — testing is hardware-in-the-loop via CAN bus tooling. Python scripts require `python-can` and `pyusb`.

## Project Conventions

### CubeMX-managed files — CRITICAL
Files generated by STM32CubeMX ([main.c](Core/Src/main.c), [main.h](Core/Inc/main.h), [stm32l4xx_it.c](Core/Src/stm32l4xx_it.c), [stm32l4xx_hal_msp.c](Core/Src/stm32l4xx_hal_msp.c), [freertos.c](Core/Src/freertos.c)) use `/* USER CODE BEGIN */` / `/* USER CODE END */` markers. **Only edit inside these blocks** — everything outside is overwritten on regeneration from [BMS-Firmware-RTOS.ioc](BMS-Firmware-RTOS.ioc).

### Memory constraints
Only 12KB FreeRTOS heap, 64KB flash. Stack sizes are tightly tuned (512B most tasks, 1024B CAN). Avoid dynamic allocation outside task creation. No `printf` or UART — all debug output goes through CAN messages.

### I2C robustness
All I2C operations include bus recovery (GPIO-level SCL toggling + STOP condition). HAL return values are always checked against `HAL_OK`.

### File organization pattern
Each module follows: Includes → Private defines → Private types → Static variables → Static function prototypes → Public function implementations → Static function implementations.

### CAN protocol changes
When modifying CAN message definitions, update both the source in [Core/Inc/can_ids.h](Core/Inc/can_ids.h) and regenerate the DBC via [Scripts/generate_dbc.py](Scripts/generate_dbc.py). The DBC covers 6 modules (`BMS_Module_0`–`BMS_Module_5`).

## Integration Points
- **BQ76952** register map: [Core/Inc/bq76952.h](Core/Inc/bq76952.h) — 400+ register defines. Subcommand access uses `CommandOnlySubcommand()` / `DirectCommand()` patterns in [Core/Src/bq_handler.c](Core/Src/bq_handler.c).
- **Thermistors**: 7 ADC channels × 8 MUX channels, 12-sample oversampling. NTC 10kΩ/B3435. Indices 54-55 are ambient (excluded from cell min/max). See [Core/Src/cell_temp_handler.c](Core/Src/cell_temp_handler.c).
- **Config persistence**: Module ID stored in flash page. See [Core/Src/config_manager.c](Core/Src/config_manager.c) and [Docs/ConfigParameters.md](Docs/ConfigParameters.md).
- **Bootloader**: Validates magic number at `0x08007FF8`. BSS/interrupts disabled at startup before `HAL_Init()` to support warm start.
